name: Stratum Mid-Grade Analyst's Pressed Set
description: A step above the standard-issue grey, this Tier 3-adjacent outfit represents the upper ceiling of what a cubicle worker can wear without triggering HR review. The centerpiece is a Stratum-branded slim-fit dress shirt in pale slate blue, woven from a 60/40 synth-cotton coolweave blend that resists both sweat and wrinkle for a full nine-hour shift. It's paired with Stratum's mid-grade pressed trousers in charcoal with a faint pinstripe — not bold enough to read as Tier 4, but enough to signal ambition. A single-button charcoal blazer in budget synth-wool sits over the top, cut straight across the back with no tail vent — a standard cut that quietly excludes anyone with a tail modification. Shoes are clean black derby oxfords with a synthetic welt. The only personal touch allowed is a small pin or badge on the lapel — most wearers choose their department insignia. The left sleeve has a discreet chrome-channel seam for a forearm-mounted data cuff, the one concession to augmentation that Stratum's corporate dress code explicitly permits.
functionality: Coolweave moisture management for desk-to-floor transitions, chrome-channel seam in left sleeve for forearm data cuffs, wrinkle-resistant trouser finish, RFID-transparent lapel zone for badge pinning
what_it_says: This person is trying. They've bought slightly better than the company minimum, they iron their shirt, and they keep the blazer on even when it's warm. They want to be seen as Tier 4. They are not yet Tier 4. The pinstripe is a quiet declaration of intent that everyone above them finds slightly endearing and slightly irritating.
worn_by: Stratum Corp analysts angling for promotion
cubicle workers who spent their clothing budget on this one outfit
mid-floor supervisors without official supervisor titles
story_hooks: A character in this outfit is approached in the elevator by a Tier 4 exec who mistakes them for a junior specialist — the conversation that follows opens a door that was never meant for them.
The chrome-channel sleeve seam has been quietly modified by a street tailor to also carry a concealed micro-filament data tap; the wearer may or may not know it's there.

HR flags this outfit during a dress-code review — the pinstripe is technically within regulation but has been worn by three employees recently promoted out of the department, and someone senior is paying attention.

physical_description.visual_profile: A conservative, buttoned-up silhouette that reads as aggressively middle-management. The outfit projects institutional compliance with carefully calibrated hints of upward mobility. On the wearer, it creates a neat, compact figure that disappears into office environments—precisely the intention.
physical_description.fit: Slim through the torso and shoulders, with tapered legs. The blazer sits close to the body with no drape, emphasizing a straight line from collarbone to hip. Trousers break cleanly at the ankle without pooling. Everything is cut to minimize movement and maximize uniformity.
physical_description.primary_material: Dress shirt: 60/40 synth-cotton coolweave blend (moisture-wicking, permanent-press treated). Trousers and blazer: budget synth-wool with synthetic reinforcement at stress points. Shoes: synthetic leather welt construction.
physical_description.texture: Shirt has a subtle matte finish with a slight cooling sensation to the touch. Trousers and blazer feel uniform, slightly stiff from factory treatment—crisp and corporate. Shoes have a waxy sheen. No organic texture anywhere; everything engineered for durability and consistency.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pale slate blue dress shirt (corporate-approved cool tone), charcoal trousers with faint pinstripe in medium grey, charcoal single-button blazer. Black oxford shoes. The palette is deliberately muted—nothing that would stand out in fluorescent cubicle lighting.
physical_description.closures: Standard mother-of-pearl button front on shirt (6 buttons), covered button placket. Trousers feature a flat-front with a single chrome snap closure and side-zip. Blazer single-button closure with reinforced anchor point. No magnetic snaps—this is old-money conservative.
distinctive_features: Discreet chrome-channel seam running down left sleeve—a factory-integrated data cuff port for authorized forearm augmentation
Department insignia pin or badge slot on left lapel (small, mandatory for identification)
Stratum branding embossed subtly on blazer lining and waistband tag
Reinforced stress points at cuffs, collar, and armpit—designed for 40-hour weekly endurance
No tail vent on blazer—intentional exclusionary design
Pocket-free blazer front (decoration only; all functional pockets on trousers and shirt)
Synthetic welt on shoes shows zero scuff protection—signals the wearer never walks outside
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 high-end / Tier 3-adjacent aspiration. This is the ceiling of working-class corporate wear. It signals a salary in the 45-55k Φ range, with possible quarterly bonuses. Not wealthy enough for Tier 2 tailoring, but dressed above standard Tier 3 line-worker gray.
physical_description.cultural_context: Marks the wearer as a corpo drone with middle-management ambitions. The outfit says: 'I follow rules perfectly, I own one augmentation port, I show up on time, I do not threaten anyone above me.' Wearing this means you've accepted the compact—stability over personality. HR has pre-approved your existence.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine on Monday, broken-in by Wednesday. The shirt stays crisp thanks to the permanent-press blend; the trousers develop subtle knee creases; the shoes remain scuffless (carpet-only lifestyle). After six months, the blazer's shoulders show compression marks. After one year, the chrome-channel seam begins showing micro-wear. Most wearers replace this outfit annually before the damage becomes visible.

image_prompt: Corporate fashion photography: front-facing shot of a Tier 3 analyst wearing pale slate blue synth-cotton dress shirt, charcoal pinstriped trousers, and single-button charcoal blazer. Model is standing in perfect posture against a background of blurred office cubicles and cold fluorescent ceiling grid. Harsh overhead lighting emphasizes the matte texture of the fabrics and casts sharp shadows. Close-up detail shot of the left sleeve showing the chrome-channel data cuff seam running vertically down the forearm. Lapel badge is visible but generic—corporate insignia only. Black derby oxford shoes have a waxy sheen. The overall mood is sterile, purposeful, quietly oppressive. Color grading is desaturated with cool undertones. Cyberpunk aesthetic: nothing flashy, everything optimized. --ar 2:3 --v 6
